title: Scale-ratio acceptance invariants (house:band 1–2×, wide band < house footprint, role ordering) have no durable test — only re-blessable pixel goldens
evidence: view.odin:1388-1398: "// v2-scale-depth: standard 5.5 → 7.4 (band 11.2 → 15.0px at fit). The / ladder keeps its 1:1.57:2.43 ratio but caps WIDE below the house / footprint (band 21.3px < house 21.6px — a pipe must never dwarf the / node it serves; the r1 review finding). ... case \"wide\": return 10.5". sprites.odin:240-243: "sprite_house_target :: proc(v: ^View) -> f32 { return 0.90 * v.tile_px * v.scale } / sprite_host_target ... 1.15 ... sprite_small_biz_target ... 1.10 ... sprite_campus_target ... 1.40". Spec acceptance (_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-v2-scale-depth.md:72): "i.e. house:band ≈ 1.44× (down from 3.2×), campus:band ≈ 2.24× (down from 4.7×)". Grep of all *_test.odin for sprite_house_target|tier_pipe_width|house:band|shadow_for: zero matches; palcheck pins only presence floors (small_biz >120, campus >350).
detail: The acceptance ratios live only in PR prose, comments, and exact-match goldens that any deliberate re-bless overwrites. A later retune re-blessed without re-measuring silently accepts a ratio regression; no relational pin exists.
recommended_fix: Add an app/render unit test (palette_polish_test precedent) asserting house:band ∈ [1,2], wide band ≤ house footprint, and house < sbiz < host < campus ordering from the live procs.

title: Edge-water distribution (border ~45% vs interior ~30%) — the acceptance metric of the map change — is measured by no committed gate
evidence: map.odin:79-82: "// edge_bias_factor — 1 at the NEAREST border, 0 in the interior (min() of // the two axis distances, then sharpened by repeated squaring). The r1 fix: // the first cut used max() (0 at the border, ~1 at the center) which put the // suppression at the corners — interior water never dropped." Field note (_bmad-output/field-notes/packet-plumber-v2-scale-depth.md): "the first center-suppression cut was spatially INVERTED (max() of axis distances put the bias at corners, not the center) and both hunters caught it". palcheck.odin:375 pins totals only: "check(count_exact(calm, MAP_WATER) > 150_000, \"map water (D9 world water cells)\", ...)"; palcheck.odin:433: "check(h1 == MAP_IDENTITY_PIN, ...)" — an exact hash re-blessed in the same PR. Spec I/O matrix line 43: "border ~45% water vs interior ~30%".
detail: The spatial-inversion bug class occurred in this very change and was caught by review, not by a gate: identity pin and total-count floors cannot distinguish an inverted or uniform bias after a re-bless. Grep finds no border/interior measurement in harness/ or tools/.
recommended_fix: Add a palcheck leg computing border-ring vs interior water share from the generated cells (e.g., border ≥ 1.2× interior) so the edge-clustered read survives re-blesses.

title: Thumbnail gate (hard rule 3) exists only as manual PR-body numbers — no committed tool, unlike blur_gate.py
evidence: Spec task line 69: "Thumbnail gate: render a fit capture, downscale to 427×240, verify the network hero read survives smaller nodes (pixel-scan: pipe band ≥ ~5px at 427×240, node ≥ ~4px)". PR body lines 92-94: "Thumbnail gate: network-hero pixel share at 427×240 unchanged (3.31% → 3.30%); standard band 5.0px, house 7.2px at thumbnail". Grep for "427|thumbnail" across tools/, harness/, app/, core/: zero matches. palcheck.odin:3-5 origin doctrine: "The pre-PR scratch pixel-scan was disposable and it MISSED the B1 sprite-crop bug".
detail: The 427×240 hero-read acceptance was verified by a disposable scan whose numbers live only in PR prose. Nothing prevents a later scale change in the re-bless-heavy v2 wave from regressing the thumbnail read unnoticed.
recommended_fix: Commit tools/thumbnail_gate.py beside blur_gate.py: downscale a fit capture to 427×240, assert band ≥5px, node ≥4px, network-hero share floor; exit-code gate.

title: New `land` palette token lacks the unit-level load+fallback pin every recent shipped token received
evidence: palette.odin:198: "p.land = jcol(obj, \"land\", {239, 228, 186, 255}) // the v2-scale-depth warm land tint"; palette.odin:293: "p.land = {239, 228, 186, 255}" (fallback). Precedent, palette_polish_test.odin:50-56: "p := palette_load() // the embedded data/palette.json — the shipped token / expect_color(t, p.canvas, {237, 226, 200, 255}) / // the fallback copy (a broken JSON must not silently regress the token) / f := fallback_palette() / expect_color(t, f.canvas, {237, 226, 200, 255})". Grep of *_test.odin for `land`: zero pins.
detail: The load path is only transitively pinned (T2 goldens + palcheck's hardcoded {239,228,186}>150K floor); the fallback default is untested, breaking the polish-test precedent for shipped tokens.
recommended_fix: Add expect_color pins for p.land and fallback_palette().land == {239,228,186,255} to app/render/palette_polish_test.odin.
